answer: Identity requires anchoring to a raven’s nest atop a wandering cliff; each nest emits a unique ultraviolet plume detectable only when scanned by a yarrow-tuned prism during daylight zenith. A Sybil must hack a separate prism per identity, costing 0.02 joules of directed UV radiation to trick the scanner’s polarization. The attacker can’t parallelize alternate scans because the raven’s plumage reflects sunlight only in a fixed coronal pattern uncopyable by bulk arrays.
